# Code of conduct

Posnic is a small project used by people running real businesses. Treat the
people here with the same care you would want in a shop full of customers.

## Expected behaviour

- Be direct about code and kind about people. Review the change, not the
  person.
- Assume good faith, ask before assigning a motive, and correct mistakes
  plainly.
- Respect privacy. Do not publish customer data, addresses, credentials, or
  private correspondence.
- Keep discussion on the topic in hand, and take a disagreement to a smaller
  channel before it becomes a spectacle.
- Accept a maintainer's decision to close a thread or a change, even when you
  disagree with it.

## Not acceptable

Harassment, threats, discrimination, sexualised attention, doxxing, deliberate
intimidation, sustained disruption, or publishing another person's private
information without permission. This applies in issues, pull requests,
discussions, reviews, chat, and any project space.

## Scope

This code applies whenever you are representing the project or taking part in a
project space. It does not turn a technical disagreement into misconduct, and it
does not give anyone the right to police another person's identity.

## Reporting

Report a concern to the maintainer who supplied your build, or through the
private contact supplied with your distribution. Do not open a public issue
containing the details or the identity of the person affected. If the concern
is a security vulnerability, use [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) instead.

Maintainers will acknowledge a report, keep it as private as the facts allow,
and decide on a proportionate response. They may remove a comment, close a
thread, require an apology, or exclude a participant from the project. A
maintainer who is involved in the report must step out of the decision.

The governance process is in [GOVERNANCE.md](../docs/GOVERNANCE.md).
